disclaimer: These are simulated-persona reviews generated by AI agents, not interviews with real coaches. They supplement rather than replace human feedback.
expectations: I expect one staff workspace to turn game film into cuts, checked scouting and an approved unit plan, with coaches making the call.
I read this as an invite-only room for a head coach and assistants assigned to the offense, defense and special teams.
In ten minutes I expect to be looking at this week’s film, checking a suggested cut or label against its frame and seeing where my coordinator approves the plan.

tasks.title: Sign in and find this week’s work
tasks.attempted: Chose the listed head-coach account, signed in with its prefilled demo credentials, entered its MFA code and followed Schedule from the dashboard.
tasks.observed: Within the first minute the dashboard and schedule agreed on Week 10 away at Westmoor, Friday October 30 at 7:00 PM, and a 5–2 record. Open tasks included 16 proposed cuts, a rejected file, failed inference, offense and defense comments, defense v1 awaiting approval and an outstanding invitation. The game links carried Week 10. The invite was a team item without game or due-date attribution. The banner identified Head coach.

tasks.title: Inspect a model call against its frame
tasks.attempted: Aimed for Formation, opened the neighboring Play type cell for play 5, read the run rationale and followed its 10:35–10:38 evidence.

A head coach or reviewing assistant confirms the play type.

ai_evidence.scope: Head coach in a fresh signed-in Chromium mock session, using Week 10 at Westmoor. G2/G3 covered the latest Caldwell asset (no plays at first view), Stonebrook (48 timeline entries, one coach split, 96 identifiable model labels on plays 1–12, 288 later cells explicitly marked no model output), and the later synthetic upload (3 heuristic cuts; no model labels). Reviewed cards repeated across different selected report bases are identified by that filter. Seven playbook extractions and twelve plan items recognizably invoking scouting were checked, including one manual transcription. Other plain coach plan calls carried no identifiable AI attribution and were not treated as new model predictions. No distinct recommendation workflow surfaced. The film-review prototype was not entered in this head-coach path. The signed-out context was used only for H5/W1. Repeated evidence checks after W1 did not add task or W1 steps. Separate post-seal comparison checks used the same listed role in a new mock context for reproducible version histories. The exact approved mixed-source defense line was revisited without counting a duplicated exposure. The later reset was explicit and took place after the remaining comparisons.

interview.answer: I could see the Westmoor game, the defense approval and the open comments before I had to open a single film.

I expected film evidence and a coordinator approval trail. The versions gave me the trail. The run label opened a credited substitute, and I could not find a plan-sharing control on the version I approved.

Sunday I check my seven assistants’ outstanding decisions, agree the install with the coordinators, then make sure the right people can see it. The dashboard and defense v1 start that conversation. I would keep the shared planning sheet for owners and the existing access system for a parent request.
I saw Draft saved beside an unadded Short yardage line. Switching units brought my text back, so I thought it would be there after Submit for review. The approved section was empty.

I trusted that the head-coach reason had been recorded because I reopened the version and read it. Play 5 called a run and cited a handoff, but the player told me the credited clip was a stand-in. I would need the Westmoor snap before using that call with an assistant.
I would stop using it as our plan of record if ordinary submission let a typed coaching point disappear. If we upload identifiable film, I also need to be able to act on a removal request.
I would first make Submit flag every unadded entry and let me include it. Second, I would give the staff an approved version with an audience, expiry and revocation I can verify before sending it.
I would keep the original approval on a superseded version, the separate head-coach reason and the date on each. I would also keep the honest warning that the clip is a stand-in.

I would use it conditionally, once submitting a plan accounts for my pending entries and we can trace and control the version we distribute. I would recommend it to the staff conditionally, after I can show a real snap behind a call and verify film removal and plan access.
I could invite one defensive assistant and still see the role, unit and expiry after reload. That is a piece of staff administration I would trust someone to learn on their first Sunday.

I would consider switching from Hudl, our planning sheet and the school calendar for a single trace from Sunday film to Monday’s approved version. I still had to copy the 9-of-11 finding by hand, and the approved sentence had no route back.
I would open the dashboard on my own to see which unit is in review. I would follow up with the coordinator outside it before treating the Sunday check as finished.

I would measure the share of Monday installs for which every pending coaching point is accounted for in the approved version before staff receive it. I would set a target of 100 percent for a four-game trial.

findings.title: Approved plans do not expose sharing or revocation
findings.element: Approved offense v4, version chooser and plan footer
findings.observed: An approved version was readable in the signed-in head-coach session and its ordinary workspace route sent the signed-out session to Sign in. No share creation, audience preview, expiry, active links or revoke control was available on the approved version, Staff or Settings.
findings.expected: The head coach should be able to demonstrate who can open a specifically shared version, for how long and how access can end.
findings.proposed_change: Add version-specific sharing with a visible audience, expiry and revocation history that can be checked from a signed-out browser.
findings.quote: I can prove my address bar requires sign-in. I cannot answer the parent asking whether their link will still work tomorrow.
findings.weekly_cost: Every weekly distribution creates a privacy decision the head coach must make in a different tool, and access cannot be withdrawn through this screen.

findings.title: Timestamped film claims resolve to a labeled stand-in
findings.element: Play 5 Play type evidence and film player
findings.observed: The 10:35–10:38 run citation selected play 5 in the correct asset and gave an explicit stand-in notice. The credited clip could not show the alleged Westmoor handoff. This also affected positive labels, auto cuts and scouting timestamp destinations checked separately. The specific former cut, provenance and scouting controls were retested: play 32 at 68:23, play 5 at 635.7 seconds, and current supporting 40:35 on play 19. Each named the intended original interval while playing the same 6.34-second credited play-1.mp4.
findings.expected: A coach using these calls to sign a plan needs the identified Westmoor snap, with the existing honest availability notice if it is unavailable.
findings.proposed_change: Provide original matching demo evidence for representative decisions and retain explicit availability and identity at every seek.
findings.quote: The clock is on the right snap. Show me our handoff before I sign off on the run call.
findings.weekly_cost: With no original visual evidence, every weekly film-derived decision requiring confirmation has to be checked in another film system before install.

findings.title: A head coach cannot remove a disposable film from its asset page
findings.element: Film list and detail for the synthetic upload
findings.observed: The 2 KB synthetic file survived reopening. Job Cancel was present during processing; the subsequent Ready page offered cut and model controls and no per-asset deletion or audit. The retention-setting text described an explicit deletion action.
findings.expected: A head coach should be able to confirm a particular deletion, see its consequences and verify removal and an audit record.
findings.proposed_change: Expose an audited per-asset deletion with confirmation on the film details and a verifiable result in the list and former route.
findings.quote: If the school asks me to take down this clip, changing the retention number does not answer the request.
findings.weekly_cost: A removal request may arrive in any game week. Delaying it leaves the file available and the athletic director with no evidence that the request was acted on.

findings.title: Submit for review leaves pending Add text out of the immutable plan
findings.element: Short yardage Add field and Submit for review
findings.observed: The v3 pending field was recoverable after a unit switch and labeled not added. Submit then made the version read-only with Short yardage (0) and gave no discard decision. The text was absent after approval/reload and from the next draft; explicitly re-entering it, adding and saving worked in v4.
findings.expected: Submitting a draft with pending coach input should identify the affected section and require including or knowingly discarding the text.
findings.proposed_change: Require a per-transition choice to add or discard outstanding field text before making the version read-only.
findings.quote: I had already typed the Monday scout card. I expected to see it when I put my name on the plan.
findings.weekly_cost: A typed weekly instruction can be omitted at the deadline. The head coach had to retype the same 9-of-11 card for v4 after approving an empty v3.

findings.title: A reviewed trips example conflicts with its linked play’s reviewed label
findings.observed: The 19/54 reviewed trips card described its 4:10 example as “Trips right, 1st and 10.” It opened Stonebrook play 2, whose grid showed a coach correction to doubles and an abstained Down. Its other example, play 15 at 32:00, showed no model output in the grid. Both images were stand-ins. This establishes a mismatch in the first cited example, not that the overall fraction is numerically wrong.
findings.expected: A play listed as supporting a reviewed claim should agree with the current reviewed labels and identify any unavailable situation evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Reconcile supporting examples with current coach-reviewed labels and remove or explain conflicting citations.
findings.quote: My staff corrected that play to doubles. I need an explanation before I use it as the trips example.
findings.weekly_cost: Using a contrary reviewed example risks a mistaken weekly installation decision even if the source video is eventually supplied; staff have to reconcile the correction and report outside the card.

findings.title: A defense rewrite has an author but no assigned owner
findings.element: Open tasks, defense-plan comment and Staff membership
findings.observed: The Week 10 Sunday task opened a head-coach comment asking for the third-down note to be reworded. The destination named its author, not the person responsible for the rewrite. Staff listed one active defense/special-teams coordinator; nothing on the task connected that member to the requested work. The same path was repeated in a fresh comparison session.
findings.expected: The person responsible for an open decision should be evident on the scoped task and its destination.
findings.proposed_change: Display the assigned owner and next action on an open plan task and its destination.
findings.quote: I know who normally coordinates defense. I need to know who took this particular rewrite.
findings.weekly_cost: A missing owner can delay Monday install. Sunday staff can recover by calling the unit coordinator, which adds a separate hand-off.

findings.title: The Week 10 dashboard omits an existing film queue from its proposed count
findings.element: Open tasks count after the second ready film
findings.observed: The dashboard initially showed 16 proposed cuts. After the upload completed it showed 3, while the original Week 10 Stonebrook asset still showed 16 proposed and the new asset showed 3. The dashboard gave no filename or qualifier for the displayed three.
findings.expected: A weekly work total should include all applicable assets, or tell the coach which asset a partial count describes.
findings.proposed_change: Show either the full game cut count with per-asset breakdown or an explicitly scoped count for each file.
findings.quote: If I tell the staff there are three left, somebody still has sixteen cuts on the old film.
findings.weekly_cost: When a second file arrives, the head coach could close the Sunday review with outstanding work omitted from the displayed task. Opening each asset is a possible but repeated check.

findings.title: A mixed-basis tendency passes whole-plan approval without an item decision
findings.element: Defense v2 Opponent tendencies, draft, review and approval; offense v4 manual scouting item
findings.observed: In the independent offense v4 path, a copied 9/11 scouting statement was saved with no finding or decision link. The original-case recheck then followed the seeded equivalent in defense v2: “Run on second and 3 or fewer (9 of 11; includes unreviewed labels)” appeared in the draft, in review, and in the reopened approved version. The head coach approved the whole version with a reason. No control on that item linked to a recommendation or recorded a decision about the mixed source.
findings.expected: The head coach should be able to distinguish whole-version approval from a deliberate, traceable decision on an input that includes unreviewed labels.
findings.proposed_change: Let staff bring the cited finding into a pending plan proposal and preserve the human decision and source on the approved item.
findings.quote: I can read my sentence back. I cannot take the AD back to the decision that put it there.
findings.weekly_cost: Hand transcription and looking up the originating report recur during each install; the coaching sheet is a viable workaround but does not preserve the decision chain.

findings.title: The saved retention period does not establish the removal date
findings.element: Media retention form and current setting
findings.observed: Settings changed from 365 to 180 days and stayed at version 2 after reload. The screen described explicit deletion and a separate 24-hour unfinished-upload timeout, but did not identify a starting date, whether existing media follows the new period or whether it is eligibility or automatic deletion.
findings.expected: The head coach should be able to explain how a particular already-uploaded film will be affected by a policy change.
findings.proposed_change: State the start event and scope of the saved policy and show a film’s eligibility or scheduled removal date when available.
findings.quote: I can repeat 180 days. I cannot tell a parent which day the October film becomes eligible to go.
findings.weekly_cost: Every policy change or family question needs a separate administrative check; the saved value alone cannot settle an existing film’s retention.

findings.title: A failed inference task appears in Week 11 with no film
findings.element: Linden Falls Open tasks and its film destination
findings.observed: In the post-walkthrough retest, changing the dashboard from Westmoor to Week 11 Linden Falls removed the Westmoor cuts and comments but kept the failed Infer labels task. Its link opened Week 11 film, which said “No film for this game yet.” The task did not name the affected asset or describe itself as team-wide.
findings.expected: A weekly job alert should identify the correct game and asset so staff can act on it.
findings.proposed_change: Scope the job alert and its link to the relevant game asset or label team-wide exceptions.
findings.quote: I would send an assistant to look at a failed job in a week that has no film.
findings.weekly_cost: Incorrect weekly failure alerts take recurring staff follow-up to locate the actual film; the head coach can investigate elsewhere in the season.

findings.title: Playbook extraction citations do not open the original document
findings.element: Red-zone supplement document list and proposed concept source page
findings.observed: Sprint-out Smash and Jumbo Wedge had inline OCR text and page numbers. Clicking the citation and listed document did not open a page. The Wedge excerpt said only “Wedge (OCR, low confidence)”; it did not substantiate the proposed Jumbo name. The same original-document limitation applied to the other identified extractions.
findings.expected: A reviewer deciding whether to accept or reject an extracted term should be able to inspect its source page or see that the original page is unavailable.
findings.proposed_change: Open the relevant original page from every extraction citation and retain the OCR excerpt beside it.
findings.quote: The excerpt says Wedge. I cannot approve the word Jumbo just because it appears in the proposed name.
findings.weekly_cost: A coordinator or head coach must find the installation document elsewhere to decide uncertain extractions, with particular impact when the playbook changes.

findings.title: The newest seeded asset still had no reviewable cuts during inspection
findings.element: Caldwell segment job, empty timeline and link back to the film list
findings.observed: The Oct 25 Caldwell upload showed Segment running, 38 of about 100 minutes scanned and No plays proposed yet. The independent coach opened the Oct 21 Stonebrook file to find a cut. In a clean comparison session Caldwell displayed the same progress and empty state over a 46-second observation, while Stonebrook still provided a queue. This is a bounded observation.
findings.expected: The newest demo film should offer a runnable path from processing to reviewable cuts or a clearly signposted ready alternative.
findings.proposed_change: Give the latest demo asset a segment job that produces reviewable cuts and indicates when it is ready.
findings.quote: I can assign work from last week’s usable file; I still do not have a snap from the newest upload.
findings.weekly_cost: Staff must revisit processing or use older tape before assigning cuts on the newest film. The earlier ready upload is a workaround for a demonstration.

findings.title: A dashboard cut-review task opens opponent scouting
findings.element: Open tasks link for proposed play cuts
findings.observed: The live task “3 proposed play cuts are waiting for review” opened Week 10 Opponent Scouting on the offense tab. It did not identify an asset, reviewer or a cut queue. Opening the separate defense comment did reach the relevant plan.
findings.expected: An actionable cut count should take the head coach to the associated game asset or a scoped cut queue where responsibility and state can be checked.
findings.proposed_change: Point each cut task at its matching asset and review queue, and display its scope and reviewer when assigned.
findings.quote: When it says three cuts, I expect to see those three cuts, not the opponent tendency report.
findings.weekly_cost: Each Sunday the head coach has to search the film list or ask an assistant which queue a displayed open count refers to.

findings.title: Opening an existing draft also reports that a draft was created
findings.element: Start a new draft from approved offense v1 while v2 exists
findings.observed: The retry correctly opened the existing v2 and displayed “v2 is already this unit’s open draft; opened it instead of creating another.” At the same time the success message said “Draft created.” Retrying and reloading still showed one draft.
findings.expected: The confirmation should identify whether an existing draft was opened or a new draft was created.
findings.proposed_change: Show a matching “Opened existing v2” status for an existing-draft return.
findings.quote: I can sort it out in the selector, but those two messages say different things about what I just did.
findings.weekly_cost: An occasional extra selector check resolves the contradictory confirmation. No duplicate version or lost input occurred in this path.

keep: Preserve the required head-coach override reason and the superseded-version record linking the original coordinator approval to its successor.
Keep the open invite’s role, unit and expiry visible after a reload.
Preserve the player’s explicit notice identifying a cited play/time as stand-in footage and the separate written explanation of why a label was withheld.
